why: Research walleye-slot-flip-why: a failed fastboot boot on the active slot makes Qualcomm's ABL flag it unbootable and switch to the other successful slot, which is what we saw; the kernel probably never ran. set_active is metadata only and reversible, a and b both boot Android and fastboot stays reachable, so the way back is on record (a two-way door).
rejected: set_active a now (a stays successful=no, the next failed try flips it again, a write for nothing); set_active before every try (a write per try); flashing a stub dtbo now (no known way back: the author's decision); waiting for the author (the flags are reversible and the way back is recorded).

brief: A backlog item names the device it is for; phone-next and phone-queue require --device, and lane-next gives a lane's next item of a kind (phone, research, build)
decision: backlog gains device (a devices id) and needs takes phone, research or build. The records that set needs refuse a phone, research or build item without a device (tad has no conditional rule). phone-next and phone-queue require --device; lane-next --device D --needs N gives the lane's next item, for its keeper and launchers. Filled once: open phone items in docs, surya-lab, lab-tools (about deep-sleep) and sxmo-deviceprofiles (about sx-surya) are xiaomi-surya; google-walleye-lab's and lab-tools' about google-walleye are google-walleye. The briefs, AGENTS.md and the README name the device.
why: Per-lane launchers (ideal-agent decision 2026-11-17-a-lane-starts-its-own) need a lane's next item; needs said only phone, and phone-next could hand surya's items to walleye's keeper. Orchestration (owner of docs), 2026-11-17: the device is a fact of the item, devices.id the reference; required, not optional; list what cannot be placed.
rejected: An optional --device (a walleye keeper would still take surya's items); the lane read off the project (surya's phone items live in docs, about components); a device on components (components are shared across devices); a needs value per device (needs says what kind, device says whose); a table rule (tad has none conditional yet - the records enforce it).

brief: docs keeps general knowledge for all devices; each device has its own open base; docs pulls and derives progress. one-database stays for docs and its tools.
decision: Decision 2026-11-17-one-database is superseded for devices only. Each device (surya, walleye, a third) has its own open base, made from device-template and following idealkb: queue, tries, measurements, decisions, research about it, its parts with status, evidence and date. docs holds concepts, the components and features catalogue, landscape, general decisions and research, shared sources, the tests catalogue, the lab tooling, and a registry of devices with the address of each base; support status and progress are derived from the devices' declared parts, pulled in CI, never typed or copied (stale or missing: not known yet). Lanes and launchers ask their device's own base. A third device is made from the template and registered with one record. The work to get there is on docs' backlog under commons-only, each part with its owner.
why: 40 of docs' own 81 backlog items, 34 of 49 research rows and 14 of 28 decisions name a device; test_results is 1.3 MB of 2.0 MB; the keeper's landings conflict in docs' data; the author wants docs to hold only what helps all devices. The device field and lane-next (docs 260) separate lanes but not weight or conflicts.
rejected: One database with a device field (lanes only); status typed in docs and in the device; submodules or subtrees; push from each device; CI-only derivation (a phone cannot run in CI); superseding one-database wholesale - its reasons still hold for docs and the lab tools. Full reasons: grenudi/ideal-knowledge-base decision 2026-11-17-commons-and-unit-bases.

brief: Find why the Pixel 2 refuses our images with a control image first, then host-built variants one change each; a dtbo stub only after both, on the author's word
decision: 1) A control: a public stock-format walleye image (LineageOS recovery or TWRP) through the same fastboot boot, to learn whether the phone's state or our image causes Load Error. 2) Host-only rebuild of the image on the pmaports blueline recipe (second offset 0, os word 0, short cmdline) and a dts with qcom,board-id/pmic-id read from the stock walleye dtb, tried one change at a time. 3) Only if both still end in Load Error, a stub dtbo in dtbo_b - a write with a recorded way back, needing the author's word.
why: Nothing reported on a Pixel 2 booting mainline; the image format already equals what pmaports boots on Pixel 3; Load Error is also given to known-good TWRP in a bad state, so a control separates state from content cheaply and with no write; the board-id change costs nothing on the host; the dtbo stub is the one proven fix on taimen (kcxt) but changes the phone.
rejected: Flash a stub dtbo first (kcxt's way): proven on taimen only, a write, and the cause may be state or ids; Read slot b's dtbo or boot header via Android first: needs set-active/boot of Android, which flips slot flags; Keep trying more offset variants (a/b style): both offset sets already behave the same under Load Error, so offsets are not the lever; Download Google's factory image to read ids: a proprietary download needing a decision, when LineageOS's public build holds the same header and dtb ids.

brief: The walleye lane may download LineageOS's official walleye boot.img as the boot control; downloads of public checksummed files are the lane's call
decision: On the author's words of 2026-11-17 ("Yes, download it"; then "no need to ask for my permission for downloads ... by roles expertise can be handled by themselves"): download LineageOS's official walleye boot.img (build 20261113, sha256 48dbc55c76ee47840e645707b6bf3ac322099c06358178ad8ddf2c6a53c17468; download.lineageos.org publishes no recovery.img for walleye: on A/B LineageOS carries the recovery in boot) from download.lineageos.org only, verify the sha256, keep it in ~/Projects/walleye-build/control/ with its URL, size and checksum recorded, read its header and dtb ids on the host (unpack_bootimg, fdtget; data, never run on the host), and boot it once from memory as the control (devlab fastboot boot now, tries on b, slot flags read before and after). Nothing is flashed. From now on downloads of public, checksummed files that the lane's work needs are the lane's decision, recorded with source and checksum; the author is asked only for his hands, a write that cannot be undone, money or outward actions.
why: Research walleye-load-error-how-it-stands: a stock-format image answers whether the Load Error is our image or the phone's state; boot.img is the smallest official file holding the true header.
rejected: TWRP or other sources (worse provenance); building a control ourselves (not a control); asking the author per download (his word: not needed).

brief: SH0 sleep vote: remove the console UART's (then the QUP) ALWAYS tags in a one-shot dtb; QMP is read-only first and off the path
decision: Chosen vector: subtract the SH0 sleep vote at its source, in the device tree. Step 1 (read only): at late suspend list which interconnect paths through qns_llcc/SH0 carry a SLEEP-bucket vote. Step 2: one-shot dtb with uart8's (debug UART) interconnect tags set ACTIVE_ONLY, console moved or the UART unbound, then cycle 15 bt-on: judged by the sleep-set flush (SH0 gone) and soc-sleeps. Step 3, only if SH0 stays: the other QUP/crypto TAG_ALWAYS nodes one at a time. If SH0 goes to zero and the counters still read 0, SH0 is cleared as a holder and the next suspects are hypotheses 2/3/6 (clocks, UFS/GDSCs, counter validity; sleep-standby-current). QMP no-ack: read-only discriminators, no change to the AOP path.
why: SH0 is the keepalive BCM of LLCC on sdm845, sm8150, sc7180 and sm7150 alike (bcm-voter forces it only in AMC/WAKE), so the sleep-set x=1,y=3 is a consumer's TAG_ALWAYS vote through qns_llcc, visible and removable in the device tree; uart8 (debug UART, avg 1 peak 1 across suspend) is the recorded candidate. It is the only non-zero sleep entry and one dtb away, while the QMP no-ack has no cheap explanation and serves only a low-ranked hypothesis. Whether SH0 blocks aosd is not known yet; the test settles it by the counters.
rejected: Fixing QMP first (the knobs only test hypothesis 5, unlikely; wiring equals sm8150, nothing points at the cause; kept as a read-only item). A late-suspend dump kernel first (a build and install for what one dtb answers; kept waiting). Zeroing SH0 by a driver patch or keepalive=false (it is by-design on all siblings and hides the consumer; the DT tag is the honest change and the one that could go upstream as a correction). Treating SH0 as a firmware latch (the sleep bucket is built only from consumer tags). Reading the Aspire 1 sleep set as proof SH0 is harmless (not measured by anyone).

brief: One reversible control on slot a: set-active a, control boot.img once, then back to b
decision: The keeper may run devlab fastboot set-active now a (metadata only), try the LineageOS control boot.img once on slot a (the state of the very first tries), record devlab's before/after report and the full fastboot text, and then set-active b if the phone ends in fastboot on a failed slot, so the phone ends as it is now (b current and successful). No flash, no dtbo or vbmeta write. Extends walleye-slot-flags-tries-on-b.
why: The control (a real stock-format image) also gets Load Error on b with a unbootable: the one change from the first tries is the slot state; set-active is metadata only, a's image is untouched and both slots boot Android, fastboot stays reachable - a recorded way back.
rejected: Flashing a stub dtbo or vbmeta (no known way back); waiting for the author (a two-way door: the lane's call); leaving the slot question open while only researching (a cheap test answers it).

brief: Restore the first state (Android booted on slot a, then bootloader) and try the control; then cold restart, host checks, UART; no write
decision: Order for the keeper: (1) walleye-load-error-first-state: set-active a, let a's Android finish booting, adb reboot bootloader, the control once; (2) walleye-load-error-restart-host if refused; (3) walleye-load-error-uart with the author's cable; writes (dtbo, vbmeta) come back as new items with their way back after those.
why: The control on slot a was refused too, so the slot flags alone are out; the only accepted image was tried from a phone that had booted Android on a normally, and that state (a successful=yes, bootloader entered from Android) is the one thing not repeated since. It writes nothing and set-active b is the way back.
rejected: Flash a stub dtbo or vbmeta now: no way back for the stock dtbo and no evidence it is the cause. Change the image again: the Lineage control already fails with a stock header. Treat the string as one fault: reports show restart, cable, set_active and reflash all cure it, so each is a separate small try.

brief: After 'Booting OKAY' with no start, bisect from the accepted stock control, not UART or a dtbo write
decision: Our images e and b are accepted from the first state but never start; the stock control boots. The next step is a bisect: images s1 (stock kernel + stock dtb + our initramfs), s2 (our kernel + stock dtb), s3 (stock kernel + our dtb), one swap each, built from the control's own unpacked parts; the keeper tries them from the first state. UART (the author's cable) and a dtbo/vbmeta write come after, only if the bisect leaves the question open.
why: A bisect uses only what we can read and rebuild on the host, changes nothing on the phone, and s1 may give a working USB shell on the stock kernel with our initramfs, a real foothold; research walleye-own-images-e-b-first-state.
rejected: UART first (needs the author's cable, a purchase or wait); a stub dtbo or vbmeta write (no way back for the stock dtbo, no evidence it is the cause: acceptance already happens); changing our images at random again.

brief: Walleye boots the vendor kernel with our gadget initramfs first (the control image, ramdisk swapped); lk2nd, a 4.4 build, UART-first as a blocker rejected
decision: Before any more tries of our own mainline images, add the method's step 3 at its cheapest: take the control (LineageOS walleye boot.img, accepted from the first state), change only its ramdisk to our gadget initramfs (172.16.43.1), keep its kernel, dtb and cmdline, and fastboot boot it from the first state. If the gadget answers, read cmdline, ids, reserved memory (ramoops, cont-splash), rails and USB mode from the running vendor kernel, read-only, and record them; only then our mainline image e/b, with the ramoops address and dts facts taken from what was read. The UART cable stays queued in parallel as the feedback channel of last resort; its oem decision is unchanged. The failing test walleye-gadget-up (by manifest serial, never VID:PID) is the proof of every step.
why: Every sibling (OnePlus 5, Mi 6, Pixel 3 XL, taimen) had a feedback channel or a known-good first; the lane has run no kernel on this phone and its one accepted image gave no sign of life. The ramdisk swap needs no kernel build and no write to the phone, uses the one image format the bootloader has accepted, and separates 'the bootloader accepts and starts it' from 'our kernel and dts are right'. It also yields the facts our dts guesses (ramoops address, simplefb, USB mode) from observation. Confirmed by main while this was written: our images e and b were accepted from the first state and neither started (walleye-own-images-e-b-first-state), so a second silent mainline try tells nothing more.
rejected: lk2nd / second stage: no msm8998 target, device list ends at msm8996, stock bootloader here is ABL not LK, maintainer closed a newer-SoC request; a port is very high cost and unproven under ABL. U-Boot under ABL (sdm845 path): no msm8998 port known, high cost. Building the vendor 4.4 kernel from GPL source: medium cost, unneeded while the Lineage image already holds a built one. Full Halium/Droidian/Ubuntu Touch install: high cost, forum reports for walleye poor, little for mainline. Going straight on with our mainline images (pmOS sibling practice): failure there tells nothing; ordered after the known-good. UART first as a gate: needs the author's hands and an oem command whose persistence is unknown (a change to the phone); kept parallel, not blocking. Flashing boot_a or a stub dtbo: writes, the author's word; only if the control and the swapped image both still end in Load Error.

brief: Floor: read the suspend entry (RSC flush, last-CPU state, interrupt rate) before any more subtraction; SH0 owner-hunt paused
decision: Read the entry before subtracting anything more. Two phone items, both read-only on the kernel (tracefs, procfs, debugfs; one 15 s cycle via way-back.sh cycle 15 bt-on with the watchdog armed): (1) floor-entry-trace: the rpmh sleep-set writes of the last CPU, the last CPU's idle state, per-CPU cpuidle and cluster genpd deltas, the interrupt delta, wakeup_sources, and every qcom_stats node before and after; (2) floor-irq-quiet: if the interrupts are not quiet, name the top sources and silence them one at a time (the pattern that fixed the same symptom on the Odin 2). Counters are treated as valid; SH0 is treated as one unexplained entry, not the blocker, and its owner-hunt (floor-sh0-owner, floor-sh0-qup-tags) pauses until the trace says whether the flush is what the AOP sees. A build item makes the interrupt check a suite test. Standby current stays the arbiter of last resort for counter validity.
why: The counter files exist because their names were read from the RAM, ddr_stats passed its key and moves; the awake icc read that pointed at SH0 is not the state at the flush (USB's 240000 is dropped by dwc3_qcom_suspend, the large peaks are tag 3); and every subtraction so far (DSPs, WLAN, USB, uart8) changed nothing while the three facts that decide whether the SoC can sleep at all - flush, last-CPU state, wake rate - were never read. The closest measured sibling (Odin 2) was held by an IRQ storm through a suspend that reported success. Reading is cheaper and safer than another one-shot dtb.
rejected: More owner-hunting for SH0 by tag or by unbinding drivers (three tries, no effect, and a BT-blocked cycle resets the phone); the debug late-suspend kernel first (a build, when tracefs gives the same facts without one); calling the counters broken (their names and ddr rows read fine); porting downstream lpm-levels or smp2p sleepstate (already rejected, no new evidence); the rpmh timeout debug series with cmd_db name lookup (unmerged, useful later to name holders once something is held); dwc3 skip-phy-init quirk (host-mode PHY refcount on the Odin 2; surya is a gadget and the UDC-unbound cycle changed nothing).

brief: Standby current in a real s2idle cycle is the arbiter of deep sleep; the counters and the AOP's view are clues, regulators and wakeups are the hunt
decision: The floor is judged by battery-only average current across a suspended cycle (charge_counter delta over the time, screen off, modem on), the line to match being 9 mA until Android on surya is measured. Next phone steps in order, each read-only or one change per cycle: (1) read every power-domain idle_states row and regulator_summary users before and after one cycle; (2) allow USB runtime PM (power/control auto on the PHY and controller) and read again; (3) the standby-current cycle itself. The AOP view is not chased further: the flush is sound and has no Linux-side reader.
why: The entry is in order (flush, deepest cluster state, quiet IRQs). The closest peer (pmaports#4846) shows counters can read poorly while holders are fixed one by one with no current change, and that regulators and USB, not the AOP, were what moved the draw; a measured 9 mA Droidian figure on the same generation gives a line. Only current is independent of the doubts about the counters.
rejected: Reading the AOP's log or message RAM beyond the stats (no mainline reader; downstream-only); more tracing of the flush (done: floor-entry-trace); S2RAM (rejected by floor-research-path); measuring Android by flashing surya now (changes the phone, not research's, and the miatoll figure gives a line meanwhile); treating aosd/cxsd counts as the only pass (peers show they can stay 0 while the draw is dominated by rails)

brief: Standby drain becomes the test standby-current: median of 3 runs of >=60 min, scored from the charge counter, witness unplugs
decision: Entered as a test with a witness step (the author unplugs USB), threshold 15 mA, scored as mean current from the charge_counter delta over the window (current_now only a cross-check), at least 60 min measured after a 10 min settle, Wi-Fi on, Bluetooth on and off as separate runs, screen off, samples every 30-60 s, charging samples discarded, invalid runs kept as invalid. The one-off run now prepared is the first such run (Bluetooth on).
why: Made repeatable so every kernel change is scored the same way; the charge counter avoids the wake-sample bias; see research standby-drain-as-a-repeatable-test.
rejected: A single 10 minute measurement (counter too coarse); scoring by battery percentage (least trustworthy); a name 'suitcase test' as a standard (none exists); Android's number as a gate now (not known yet).
